maya: Quick profiling heads-up — saw ~18% tail latency bump on host-side for small streaming requests after the kernel-select tweak. Flamegraph + syscall trace uploaded: https://internal/fg/4654 :eyes:
igor: Confirmed. perf samples point at heavy allocator churn in token_slab.cpp around handle_token_batch(). Also tons of tiny gRPC write() syscalls (~80-200B). Looks like fragmentation from minibatch scheduling + kernel choice mismatch.
sam: Hypothesis: kernel_select is preferring low-latency kernels that don't coalesce well for tiny seqs. Two quick mitigations: bump minibatch window to 6ms for seq<=64, and enable writev coalescing in the proxy. Can we A/B?
maya: Creating an experiment branch now. Plan: (1) prefer batch-friendly kernel for seq<=64, (2) host pretokenizer reuse pool to cut allocs, (3) proxy writev coalesce flag. Will canary on 2 nodes, collect p50/p99/p999 and alloc stats.
lia: Also add KV cache telemetry — I noticed miss-rate ticked up around the same change. If parallelism increased, evictions could be higher. Adding eviction counters + shard occupancy histograms.
ci-bot: ci: canary deploy queued -> `/deploy canary-host-alloc-opt sha=abc123` :gear:
igor: For local repro, commands that helped: `sudo perf record -F 99 -p $(pidof host-service) -g -- sleep 30` then `perf script | FlameGraph/stackcollapse.pl > out.folded` and `stackcollapse | flamegraph.pl > fg.svg`. Also `strace -c -e write -p <pid>` and `ss -m` for small write aggregation.
maya: Canary results in: p50 ~ same, p99 down ~6ms, p999 down ~18ms on canary nodes. Alloc churn down ~40%. writev coalesce reduced syscalls by ~12/syscall per request for small streams. Full logs: https://internal/logs/4654-canary
sam: Nice. Tail still not recovered fully though (99.9 shows ~11% above baseline). Next steps: tweak KV cache TTL and backpressure to reduce hot-shard eviction storm. If we can shave more tiny syscalls it's likely to normalize tail.
lia: KV heatmap shows hot keys concentrated on 2 shards — imbalance. Propose adaptive scoring: temporarily bump capacity of hot shards and soft-rebalance keys when occupancy > 85% for 30s. I added a metric patch.
igor: Also saw a small memory cap bump in canary after kernel pref change. Not huge but worth double-checking. I'll run `valgrind --tool=massif` and a leak-check on a staging replica.
maya: Rolling changes to staging with KV TTL tweak + soft-rebalance flags enabled. Running 4 stress passes (qps/seq-distribution). Owners: kernel selection -> @igor, pretoken pool -> @maya, KV rebalance -> @lia.
sam: Infra cleared for rollout if staging passes. Can we gate the prod roll on: p99 <= baseline+5ms, p999 <= baseline+20ms, no increase in mem/cpu >5%?
lia: Agreed. I'll also add an alert if shard-evictions/sec > 10 for >1m.
maya: No blockers reported from staging after two passes. Scheduling wider canary across 8 nodes tomorrow morning.
igor: Logging note: keep `perf.data` and folded stacks for failed canary runs, they helped trace a different tiny-write regression last month.
sam: If wider canary is green, we do progressive rollout and disable the kernel pref toggle as a rollback path. ETA prod decision EOD Friday.
lia: :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks all — will post a short postmortem if we hit weirdness.
